title: Implement a directed graph with cycle detection in Python
description: Greenfield Python task: implement a Graph class with add_edge, has_cycle (DFS-based), has_path (BFS), and reachable_from (BFS/DFS returning all reachable nodes).

injections.content:
from src.digraph import Graph


def test_no_cycle():
    g = Graph()
    g.add_edge(0, 1)
    g.add_edge(1, 2)
    assert g.has_cycle() is False


def test_has_cycle():
    g = Graph()
    g.add_edge(0, 1)
    g.add_edge(1, 2)
    g.add_edge(2, 0)
    assert g.has_cycle() is True


def test_has_path():
    g = Graph()
    g.add_edge(0, 1)
    g.add_edge(1, 2)
    assert g.has_path(0, 2) is True
    assert g.has_path(2, 0) is False


def test_reachable_from():
    g = Graph()
    g.add_edge(0, 1)
    g.add_edge(0, 2)
    g.add_edge(1, 3)
    assert g.reachable_from(0) == {1, 2, 3}


def test_empty():
    g = Graph()
    assert g.has_cycle() is False
    assert g.has_path(0, 1) is False

required_artifacts: Adjacency list stored as defaultdict(list) or similar
has_cycle uses DFS with in-stack tracking (three-color marking)
has_path uses BFS/DFS with visited set
reachable_from returns set of nodes reachable from src (not including src)
